# Asyra Framework

> Public, source-mapped documentation for people and AI coding agents.

This index contains 53 public Markdown pages.
Current: browser/Core composition, official 2D Preset, and engine-neutral CUSTOM composition.
Future: Headless Core and Core Kernel for non-visible and machine-facing products; no current public API or delivery date.

Create a Generic Starter project with `npx create-asyra-app@0.1.0 my-app --package-manager=npm` on Node.js 24; npm and Yarn are supported. See [Starter source and onboarding](/docs#generic-starter-source).
Use create-asyra-design-app for a ready-to-use design-tool product, or install @asyra/core for advanced composition. Use Extend for app-owned product behavior, and Customize when replacing Framework composition or providers.
Treat app domain schemas, permissions, migration, retrieval, services, and product rules as app-owned.

## Public pages

- [Asyra Framework](/docs): Build domain-owned information products whose visual, collaborative, persistent, and AI-facing capabilities remain composable.
- [Create a complete design app](/docs/start/create-design-app): Begin with the maintained Asyra Design product template and extend it as an app owner.
- [Extend Asyra with an AI coding agent](/docs/start/extend-with-ai): Map product problems to Asyra capabilities, assess adoption costs and limits, and verify bounded improvements.
- [Compose the official 2D baseline](/docs/start/preset-2d): Apply the optional official Preset before Core starts, then keep app-domain choices outside the Framework.
- [Compose only the infrastructure you need](/docs/start/custom-composition): Build a Core App with transaction publications, incremental persistence, scoped subscriptions, computation reuse and explicit lifecycle ownership.
- [Information models come before output](/docs/learn/information-models): Define app-owned information and rules without forcing it to be visible, rendered, collaborative, or AI-operated.
- [Intent enters through Features](/docs/learn/intent-and-features): Translate user or agent intent into explicit Feature sessions rather than mutating owners from UI or transport code.
- [Give every state one canonical owner](/docs/learn/canonical-state): Separate canonical model state, local derived state, projection state, and remote transport state.
- [One user intent, one transaction](/docs/learn/transactions-and-durability): Commit, roll back, undo, redo, publish, and persist one intended action through one canonical boundary.
- [Understand versioned loading and migration](/docs/learn/validation-load-migration): Use the Framework migration lifecycle while your product supplies its version history and domain-specific transforms.
- [Register projections without changing ownership](/docs/learn/projection-registration-replacement): Keep canonical information independent from render layers and engine providers, then choose the maintained customization path when a provider must change.
- [Current runtime and future Core Kernel](/docs/learn/runtime-boundaries-roadmap): Distinguish today's browser/Core composition from the researched Headless and Core Kernel direction for machine-facing products.
- [Build a custom component and schema](/docs/build/custom-schema): Register app-owned component meaning, property defaults, and validation through public Core APIs.
- [Build a transaction-safe Feature session](/docs/build/feature-session): Map start, update, end, and cancellation to exactly one intended undo commit.
- [Build a custom render boundary](/docs/build/render-boundary): Provide an engine through the public provider contract without teaching Core a renderer-specific implementation.
- [Build hierarchy and Group behavior](/docs/build/hierarchy-groups): Keep parent-child ordering canonical while group meaning and geometry policy remain app-owned.
- [Define migrations for your product](/docs/build/persistence-migration): Extend the Framework load lifecycle with your product's document versions, deterministic transforms, and unsupported-version policy.
- [Build opt-in collaboration](/docs/build/collaboration): Connect deterministic collaboration actors while the app owns transport, authorization, presence, and backend policy.
- [Build registered AI actions](/docs/build/ai-actions): Expose bounded action schemas and permissions so AI intent uses the same canonical transaction paths as people.
- [Build app-owned AI retrieval and action](/docs/build/app-retrieval-action): Let the app retrieve domain context and register actions without presenting future Headless support as current behavior.
- [Update your App with an AI coding agent](/docs/updates/index): Select official update guides, retain App-owned extensions and give a coding agent enough context for first and subsequent integrations.
- [Release History and Update Coverage](/docs/updates/history): Find per-owner release summaries, verified predecessor boundaries, prerequisites and guide corrections; report gaps and revisit deferred adoption.
- [Adopt Text Across Versions and Resume Partial Adoption](/docs/updates/text-cross-version-example-3): Frozen revision-1 input used in the completed independent modeled Text acceptance; see revision 2 for digest and definition-read clarifications.
- [Adopt Text Across Versions and Resume Partial Adoption](/docs/updates/text-cross-version-example-3-r2): Revision 2 clarifies digest algorithms and composition-time reads after independent local acceptance with 31 tests; original input and evidence remain preserved.
- [Modeled Text Framework](/docs/updates/releases/model-text-framework): Retained candidate with shared spacing default 0.5; modeled only.
- [Modeled Text App 1](/docs/updates/releases/model-text-app-1): Adopt official typography definitions and retain App extensions; modeled only.
- [Modeled Text App 2](/docs/updates/releases/model-text-app-2): Resume deferred shared spacing default adoption; modeled only.
- [Modeled Text App 3](/docs/updates/releases/model-text-app-3): Migrate App serialization to typed tracking after multiplier conversion; modeled only.
- [Adopt Official Text and Keep Your App Extensions](/docs/updates/text-official-fields-example-1-r2): Worked example, revision 2: adopt equivalent official Text fields while retaining custom metadata, actions, projections and saved data; independent local-candidate acceptance passed; published-package support and subsequent updates remain unverified.
- [Adopt Official Text and Keep Your App Extensions](/docs/updates/text-official-fields-example-1-r3): Worked example, revision 3: clarify shared defaults, browser acceptance and history limits; retain the original revision 2 independent acceptance.
- [Update Text Again and Preserve Intervening Extensions](/docs/updates/text-spacing-example-2-r1): Modeled subsequent update: adopt a new spacing default using the existing adoption record while preserving intervening rejected approval, custom data and deferred UI; fresh-AI local-candidate acceptance passed with 29 tests; not a published release comparison.
- [Update Text Again and Preserve Intervening Extensions](/docs/updates/text-spacing-example-2-r2): Worked example: revision 1 independent acceptance: 29 tests; revision 2 existing-context rerun: 34 tests, not a new independent acceptance. Retained pre-update delivery includes candidate archives and public sources.
- [@asyra/ai-agent-runtime](/docs/reference/packages/ai-agent-runtime): Optional registry, schema, permission, and execution boundary for app-approved AI actions.
- [@asyra/collaboration](/docs/reference/packages/collaboration): Optional deterministic replication adapters with app-owned network and service policy.
- [@asyra/core](/docs/reference/packages/core): The strict composition facade for Framework capabilities and lifecycle.
- [@asyra/design-system](/docs/reference/packages/design-system): Optional reusable interface components; not a Core dependency or app-domain owner.
- [@asyra/factory](/docs/reference/packages/factory): Canonical transactions, rollback, history replay, and shared change publication.
- [@asyra/feature-system](/docs/reference/packages/feature-system): Priority, exclusivity, conditions, and session lifecycle for intent handling.
- [@asyra/input-system](/docs/reference/packages/input-system): Environment-neutral semantic input registration and dispatch infrastructure.
- [@asyra/persistence](/docs/reference/packages/persistence): Storage adapter and validated load boundary with app-owned migration meaning.
- [@asyra/preset](/docs/reference/packages/preset): Optional official design-tool baseline with selectable defaults and replaceable providers.
- [@asyra/props-manager](/docs/reference/packages/props-manager): Property definitions, runtime values, schema validation, and registration lifecycle.
- [@asyra/reactive-events](/docs/reference/packages/reactive-events): Typed cross-package communication, transaction ownership, and replay-safe event routes.
- [@asyra/render](/docs/reference/packages/render): Projection, render-layer registration, interaction bridges, and renderer orchestration.
- [@asyra/render-engine](/docs/reference/packages/render-engine): Public engine-provider contract that keeps renderer implementations replaceable.
- [@asyra/render-engine-pixi](/docs/reference/packages/render-engine-pixi): Official optional Pixi provider for the current browser-based 2D baseline.
- [@asyra/scene-tree](/docs/reference/packages/scene-tree): Canonical element hierarchy, ordering, component relations, and subtree operations.
- [@asyra/selection](/docs/reference/packages/selection): Selection channels and state infrastructure without app-specific selection policy.
- [@asyra/system-context](/docs/reference/packages/system-context): Managed system-level properties and snapshots shared through canonical registration.
- [@asyra/ui-context](/docs/reference/packages/ui-context): UI-facing derived property registration and computation without canonical model ownership.
- [@asyra/utils](/docs/reference/packages/utils): Small shared public utilities without Framework state or lifecycle ownership.
- [Support, security, and release boundaries](/docs/reference/support-release): Current runtime support, candidate status, security reporting, license, migration, and publication boundaries.
- [Asyra Design as a complete product implementation](/docs/cases/asyra-design): See how one real product composes Framework infrastructure, Preset defaults, app-domain behavior, collaboration, persistence, and AI.
